Taste and see that the Lord is sweet; blessed is the man who hopes in him. Glorious things are spoken of you, city of God. The Lord will give grace and glory. The generation of the upright shall be blessed. There will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine righteous persons who have no need of repentance. A stone is heavy and sand is burdensome, but a fool’s anger is heavier than both. [Col. 0312B] A wise son is his father’s glory. Glory, honor, and peace to everyone who does good, to the Jew first and then to the Greek. Our glory is this: the testimony of our conscience. A twofold love makes human beings near to God. It is a great offense to refuse to appease one whom you have offended. It is a great destruction of the Church when provision for monasteries is neglected. The glory of worldly ornament is a great insult to the monastic life. The condition of the mind is shown by bodily gesture. The word of God is a sword sharpened on both sides, penetrating soul and body. [Col. 0312C]

He who seeks the glory of the world soon becomes so blinded that he fears no fall into guilt. The gravest and worst kind of enmity is to return evil for good. A certain kind of human piety will be impiety toward God. Whole and undisturbed joys are nowhere found on earth. To glory and take pride in temporal advantages is a sign of a foolish person. It is more glorious to endure an injury in silence than to avenge it by answering. One devoted to gluttony and luxury is compared to foolish beasts. What is freely given by God must also be freely given by human beings. [Col. 0312D]

A serious mind does not utter a doubtful judgment. A sin is grave when someone takes from it an example for sinning. Those who refuse to mourn at the proper time will eventually lament too late. One advanced in age ought also to utter weighty words. No one should make general benefits his private possessions. Those who have resolved to serve God with their whole heart should not reread pagan books. He gives gifts pleasing to God who breaks wicked vows. One who rejoices in the Lord tastes the sweetest honey. A people ignorant of God must be handed over to everlasting punishment. A great crime must be overcome with great zeal. [Col. 0313A]

The glory of the world is not to be loved at all. God’s grace alone makes those whom he wills worthy of attaining high things.

## CHAPTER VIII

Man is like grass; his days are like a flower of the field. When man was in honor, he was compared to foolish beasts and became like them. Man has become like vanity; his days pass like a shadow. Trust in the Lord with all your heart. Man sees the face, but God looks into the heart. An inheritance hastened toward at the beginning will lack blessing at the end. Honor the Lord from your substance, and give to the poor from the firstfruits of your crops. Man is born for labor, and a bird for flight. [Col. 0313B]

Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, so that he may exalt you at the time of visitation. God loves a cheerful giver. It is already time for us to rise from sleep. After one and then a second admonition, avoid a heretical person. It is dreadful to fall into the hands of God. This is to depart completely from evil: no longer to wish to sin, out of love for God. It is human to sin, but diabolical to persist. Everyone ought to turn to good with the same zeal with which he practiced evil. Did he cling continually to evil? Let him turn and do the same in good. [Col. 0313C]

“Honor and dominion, if you wish to have them, I will give you great ones.” Honesty and sobriety are to be sought in all things. Honor shown to God makes those who show it worthy of eternal glory. To honor parents concerns all human beings. The mysteries of the divine law are open to the humble and faithful, but hidden from the proud and faithless. To fear human beings more than God is not Christian religion. A spiritual friend is an heir and a relative. “[The wording is corrupt:] A pleasing offering to God—you will not be able to [identify] better things; hold fast to willing what is good, and seek to harm no one.” Very often the last become first. [Col. 0313D]

Remember to appease quickly those whom you have injured. He wages dreadful wars who despises the treaties of peace. Love an enemy for the Lord’s sake, but also love him as dear in himself. He shall be venerated who continually seeks what is best. Alas, how rare faith is now found among all! Those clinging to the earth cannot be subjected to contemplation.

## CHAPTER IX

The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord. Good understanding belongs to all who fear him. The wicked walk around. The Lord is near to those who are troubled in heart, and he will save the humble in spirit. The judgments of the Lord are true, justified in themselves. [Col. 0314A]

The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him and will rescue them. Cast your care upon the Lord, and he himself will nourish you. In God we shall act valiantly, and he will bring our enemies to nothing. You are righteous, Lord, and your judgment is upright. The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree and multiply like a cedar of Lebanon. The righteous will be in everlasting remembrance; he will not fear an evil report. In your patience you will possess your souls. The path of the righteous proceeds like shining light and grows until perfect day. A very strict judgment will be carried out upon those who rule. [Col. 0314B]

When the wicked comes into the depths of sins, he despises them. Wisdom will not enter a malevolent soul, nor dwell in a body subjected to sins. Through the devil’s envy death entered the world. Hell and destruction are before the Lord; how much more the hearts of human beings! Among the proud there are always quarrels; but those who do everything with counsel are governed by wisdom. The righteous lives by faith. In all your works remember your last things, and you will never sin. The beginning of every sin is pride. At the end of a person his works are exposed. In the day of good things, do not forget evil things. [Col. 0314C]

In much talk sin will not be absent. Every idle person is occupied with desires. In every place the eyes of the Lord observe the good and the evil. In everything let us present ourselves as ministers of God. The invisible things of God are seen and understood through the things that have been made. God chose the weak things of the world to confound the strong. The beginning of good things is confession of evils. The flesh is afflicted in vain if the mind does not resist pleasures. He does not lose the name “righteous” who continually rises again through repentance. Fasting is not perfect virtue but the foundation of many virtues. [Col. 0314D]

A perverse intention deserves to be permitted to wander in the daytime as in the night. Human justice is so fragile that it consists rather in the remission of sins than in the perfection of virtues. True innocence is that which harms neither itself nor others. When an angry person ceases to be angry with others, then he is most angry with himself. An angry person pleases no one, even if he raises the dead. The wicked are more unfortunate when they have accomplished what they desired than if they had been unable to fulfill their desires. Those who inflict injury are more unfortunate than those who suffer it. [Col. 0315A]

Earnest supplication prevents a pure heart from sleeping. A person sins in this very thing: that he would wish to sin if he could do so with impunity. It is useless frequently to see those things by which you are soon drawn toward every evil. God must be invoked continually, so that he may deign to grant us both the will and the ability to act well. To love enemies is indeed a difficult commandment, but its reward is great. The longer the fire of carnal desire is permitted to burn, the more difficult it is to extinguish. Small sins are forgiven those who have wept strictly over greater sins. One ungrateful person harms many wretched and poor people. He gives a double benefit to the needy who gives quickly. [Col. 0315B]

The poor lack little; the avaricious lack everything. He labors in vain in many things who strives to offer his possessions to God more than himself. The imprudent soldier boasts in peacetime that he is brave. We are permitted to suffer all the troubles of diabolical temptation so that we may learn to sympathize and grieve with all who suffer the same troubles. Chastity is difficult to preserve amid banquets. It is impossible to enjoy an abundance of pleasures without pleasure. The wicked and hard-hearted must be severely rebuked at the very beginning of sin. We must continually consider how great God’s grace is with us and how much richer we have become in bodily and spiritual gifts. [Col. 0315C]

He labors in vain who honors a blind man. In the midst of evils, the innocent most often hope for good things. The venerable patience of Job must continually be considered as an example for all who grieve and are ill. Weakness of the flesh, if endured patiently, is like a purifying fire. Almost all the weak wish to be tolerated by others, but themselves refuse to tolerate others. Divine judgment does not err, as human judgment often does. The envious person is struck first by the weapon of his own envy. Those undertaking a long journey need greater foresight than those traveling nearby. So too monks, continually serving God, need more provision than the others who live freely. [Col. 0315D]

A finite labor, however great it may be, cannot be compared with infinite labor. Glory awaits those who undertake arduous struggles. Nothing is found more harmful to a young person than following his own will. He greatly injures the Creator who loves any creature more than him. Many may be praised as wise in some respects, but in certain respects they are sometimes to be praised less. Eternal pain and torment will seize those who are now captivated by immoderate joy. Accumulated money either rules each person or serves him. The envious person wastes away at another’s prosperous circumstances. [Col. 0316A]

For those placed in mourning, music is not sweet. Anger prevents the mind from seeing the truth. Whoever strives after every impious thing cannot be prudent in the end. Full of envy, he is poorer than all. The future life must be weighed with immense care. A harsh judgment will come upon these scepters [or rulers]. Everyone will be severely tested by the Lord’s gifts. God’s hardening means nothing other than not showing mercy. Flesh grown fat rarely tastes heavenly things.

## CHAPTER X

Charity is not to be extorted from anyone, but sought through acts of kindness. Charity covers a multitude of sins. No one ought to place his dear ones before Christ.

## CHAPTER XI

[Col. 0316B]

Let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice. The righteous shall rejoice in the Lord and hope in him, and all the upright in heart shall be praised. Light has risen for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart. The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. Broad and spacious is the way that leads to death. Let your light shine before human beings, so that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven. The law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. Let us lift our hearts and hands to God. A wicked ruler over a poor people is a roaring lion and a hungry bear. [Col. 0316C]

The tongue of the wise adorns knowledge. A despised lamp, in the thoughts of the rich, is prepared for an appointed time. A soothing tongue is a tree of life. Let another praise you, and not your own mouth. Speak truth, each one with his neighbor, for we are members of one another. The letter kills, but the spirit gives life. An invading wolf shows with what disposition each shepherd had stood watch over his flock. The eye is the lamp of the body; spiritual wisdom is the light of the mind. If the tongue is not restrained, it does not merely remain where it has fallen but continually slips toward worse things. [Col. 0316D]

Unavoidable snares are prepared for those who take no care to amend their sins. Tears do not ask for forgiveness but merit it. Many places and regions have been utterly destroyed by the wickedness of their inhabitants. Hard work conquers all things. Greedy for human praise, he despises the gift of divine recompense. Constant labor suppresses carnal passions. An unusual illness seeks an unusual kind of medicine. A person is to be called free in whom no vice rules. Joyful things corrupt some people more than sad things. [Col. 0317A]

Through long practice one must learn what it is fitting for each person to say and to keep silent about. Flee shameful profit as though it were loss. Profit cannot be made without another’s loss. A fickle and unstable person differs in nothing from birds. The virtue of abstinence drives away the impulse of lust. Even if many people approve of your life, you ought not approve of it yourself. Nothing suppresses hidden pride more than an open fault. The falls of some people draw them toward better things with greater fervor, the worse the things they have committed. A wanton young man needs to be admonished frequently. Do not dissolve ancient laws by transgressing them. He rightly praises God who truly loves him. [Col. 0317B]

The tongue reveals what patience is proper to a man. He remains worthy of praise who strives to be kind. The power of the mind grows weak through excessive fatness of the belly. Eternal light belongs to the devout; darkness is always the lot of the wicked. The reading of holy books must be valued greatly. He girds his loins who restrains the desires of the flesh.

## CHAPTER XII

Great is our Lord, and great is his power, and his wisdom is without number. Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised, and there is no end to his greatness. The earth is full of the mercy of the Lord. God is wondrous in his saints. Great are the works of the Lord, sought out according to all his desires. [Col. 0317C]

The mercy of the Lord is from eternity and unto eternity upon those who fear him. The sinner borrows and does not repay; but the righteous has mercy and gives. God loves mercy and truth. The tribulations of the righteous are many, and the Lord will deliver them from them all. Many are the scourges of the sinner, but mercy will surround the one who hopes in the Lord. The death of sinners is most evil, and those who hate the righteous will sin. Better is a little possessed by the righteous than the many riches of sinners. The Lord is compassionate and merciful, patient and exceedingly merciful. [Col. 0317D]

No one has greater love than to lay down his life for his friends. Many are called, but few are chosen. The harvest is indeed plentiful, but the laborers are few. The hired servant sees the wolf coming, abandons the sheep, and flees. Obedience is better than sacrifices. The wounds of one who loves are better than the deceitful kisses of one who hates. A patient person is better than a strong man, and one who rules his spirit is better than one who captures cities. Better is a dry morsel with joy than a house full of sacrifices with strife. [Col. 0318A]

A man’s wickedness is better than a woman who does good. Better to be humbled with the meek than to divide spoils with the proud. Music during mourning is an untimely story. It is better to go to a house of mourning than to a house of feasting. It is better to be rebuked by a wise person than to be deceived by the flattery of fools. Death and life are in the power of the tongue. The memory of the righteous is with praises, but the name of the wicked will rot. Remember your Creator in the days of your youth. Cursed is the person who performs God’s work negligently. Human life upon earth is warfare, and his days are like the days of a hired laborer. [Col. 0318B]

The world and its desire pass away, but whoever does the will of God remains forever. A little leaven corrupts the whole lump. The continual prayer of the righteous is very powerful. It is better to marry than to burn. It is better not to have something to give than shamelessly to ask for something to give. It is better to be defeated well than to conquer badly. It is better to possess all lesser goods than one great good with a great evil. It is better to have holy rusticity than sinful eloquence. It is better to do first what is fitting than afterward to repent of an evil deed. It is better to divorce a human being than God. [Col. 0318C]

It is not a lie when we speak mystically of insensible things as though they were sensible. He celebrates the Sabbath badly who is idle from good works. A large part of understanding is knowing what you do not know. It is both astonishing and grievous that many, abstaining from certain foods as though they were religious, immediately strive in every way to do the worst things as though they were criminals. It is equally astonishing and grievous that many, pretending to visit holy and distant places for the forgiveness of sins, become much worse than before when they return. Many illnesses arise from excessive satiety. The character and pursuits of rulers are discerned from the quality of their subjects. [Col. 0318D]

Curses directed against neighbors first turn back upon those who utter them. A mind intent upon visible things cannot see invisible ones. Greater crimes should be believed only slowly when they are heard, but punished more quickly when they are truthfully recognized. A teacher must first be cleansed, and thus he will be able to cleanse others. A prostitute and worldly prudence are alike in many sins. Monks and clerics ought to avoid worldly business. The hands of the poor are Christ’s treasury. [Col. 0319A]

A soft and dissolute person should be called not a man but a woman. A woman devoted to virtue may be called a man. The first and greatest virtue of women is chastity. It is great security of heart not to desire what belongs to another. The courage of any soldier is not recognized except in war. To return evil for evil is human; but evil for good is diabolical. A death preceded by a good life is not to be considered an evil death. When an evil person pretends to be good, he is at his worst. An evil conscience never rests securely. Through bad rule the highest authority is lost. A very great reward will be bestowed from heaven upon those [Col. 0319B] who suffer every danger for righteousness. One dead to this world knows nothing except how to live for Christ. Great peace of mind is to avoid the affairs of the world. It is a great struggle for a young person to conquer the flesh. The greatest plague occurs when the shepherd is childish. A light and fragile mind quickly produces scandals of the flesh. A mind accustomed to evil is scarcely torn away from it. Blind lust must be called death and destruction. An evil death will be conquered if it is continually feared beforehand. Have you found honey? Be content with as much as is sufficient for you. Seek above all what will always have to be retained.

## CHAPTER XIII

The Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the path of the wicked will perish. Do not envy one who prospers in his way, a man who practices injustices. A king is not saved by great strength. Do not become like the horse and the mule, which have no understanding. Do not hope in iniquity, and do not covet robberies. Unless the Lord guards the city, the watchman keeps watch in vain. Do not trust in princes, in human beings, in whom there is no salvation. Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God. No one is good except God alone. [Col. 0319D]

Unless someone is born again of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. No one can serve two masters. No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God. A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, nor a bad tree good fruit. It is necessary that scandals come; but woe to that person through whom the scandal comes! A disciple is not above his teacher. Nothing is covered that will not be revealed, and nothing hidden that will not be known. Praise is not fitting in the mouth of a sinner. Do not delay turning to the Lord. [Col. 0320A]

Do not neglect the Lord’s discipline, and do not grow weary when you are rebuked by him. Do not rebuke a scoffer, lest he hate you; rebuke a wise person, and he will love you. Do not place a stumbling block before the blind. There is no righteous person on earth who does good and does not sin. The righteous knows the souls of his beasts, but the inner parts of the wicked are cruel. Nothing happens on earth without a cause. A friend is not recognized in prosperity, nor an enemy hidden in adversity. The Lord knows those who are his. Let no one seek only what is his own, but also what belongs to another. [Col. 0320B]

Do not be surprised if the world hates you. Not only those who do evil are guilty, but also those who consent to the evildoers. No one can say, “Lord Jesus,” except in the Holy Spirit. No one will be crowned except the one who has competed lawfully. Neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but God, who gives the growth. Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good. Do not love the world or the things that are in the world. Let us not love in word or tongue, but in deed and truth. It is not hearers but doers of the law who will be justified. God is not a respecter of persons; but in every nation whoever fears God and practices righteousness is acceptable to him. [Col. 0320C]

The love of God is never idle. Shining skin reveals a filthy mind. Nothing is more unfortunate than the prosperity of sinners. God never abandons the mind that truly acknowledges its sins. It is not a secure joy to know much in the divine books, but to keep what one has learned. It benefits no one to walk about at times with a sad face, displaying fasts, and then live in luxury. It is not enough for us to leave our possessions unless we also leave ourselves. It is not the multitude of sins but impiety that leads a person to despair. [Col. 0320D]

To know and to be able to do things previously unknown and impossible demonstrates the gifts of heavenly grace. Things that may seem small are not to be despised, without which great things cannot stand. Nothing is so easy that it does not become difficult if you do it unwillingly. No one sins against another before sinning against himself. No one should think that he deserves less punishment for sinning because he imitates a multitude of sinners. The wickedness of the devil, which is said to have been against Job, will be against all human beings if it is permitted to proceed so far. He scarcely knows what labor is who has never striven against spiritual wickedness. [Col. 0321A]

All who seem wise to themselves must take care not to be wiser than they ought. The negligent and lukewarm must be admonished in various ways. Negligence and idleness draw a person to destruction. What is believed easily repairable is usually guarded less carefully. A person’s life is not in his own power. Unless someone is founded in faith and hope, he does not ascend to the heights of true charity. No exhortation to virtue is like the remembrance of sins. Christians are not judged by their beginnings but by their end. Nothing happens to anyone, whether badly or well, for that person alone, but so that others may simultaneously be corrected or consoled through him. [Col. 0321B]

There is no evil of which God does not make use for some good. No one harms the Church more than one who, acting perversely, holds authority. It will benefit no one to be considered holy when he is not. The splendor of costly garments separates one from the kingdom of heaven. It is an exceedingly grievous presumption that Christians presume to do the evils which pagans abhor: Christians destroy the monasteries of their God and his saints, while pagans venerate their idols. No one is noble except the one whom virtue ennobles. [Col. 0321C]

Unless someone continually sets the fear and love of God before himself, he quickly falls into some sin. To know or care about nothing is to live while dead. Ask for nothing that you are going to refuse. No one sins more dangerously than one who defends sins. No one can measure himself sufficiently unless he considers another. Do not live one way in solitude and another way in public. He denies it to himself who seeks what is difficult. Nothing is great among human affairs except a mind that despises great things. Impose on no one what you cannot endure yourself. No one placed in the world renounces it securely. [Col. 0321D]

Neither human beings nor gold can make anyone blessed; rather, the blessed are so by the power of God. The eyes do not sin if the mind wishes to rule them. It cannot be said how great the enemy’s art is. Do not consider anything accomplished when something remains to be done. It is useless to have learned what is good unless you do it. Do not wish to delay if you can convert someone. No one is crowned unless he earns it by struggle. A person should not be praised for knowing much, but for living well. The striving of fools always loves an equal among companions. If there is no battle, no victory will come.

## CHAPTER XIV

The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears are attentive to their prayers. [Col. 0322A] The mouth of the righteous will meditate wisdom, and his tongue will speak judgment. The sinner will observe the righteous and gnash his teeth at him. The Lord has done everything he willed, in heaven and on earth, in the sea and in all the depths. Every kingdom divided against itself will be desolated. Everything is possible for one who believes. Every planting that the heavenly Father has not planted will be uprooted. Everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin. Everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened. Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted. [Col. 0322B]

Every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and cast into the fire. To everyone who has, it will be given; but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away. Every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven human beings, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven. Pray that your flight may not take place in winter or on the Sabbath. Bless God at all times, and ask him to direct your ways. For every undertaking there is a time and an opportunity. Guard your heart with all vigilance, because from it life proceeds. He who wishes to withdraw from a friend seeks opportunities. Do everything with counsel, and after doing it you will not repent. [Col. 0322C]

All wisdom is from the Lord God, and was always with him. Hatred stirs up quarrels, but charity covers all offenses. All flesh is grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the field. One and the same Spirit accomplishes everything, distributing to each as he wills. Whatever you do in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him. Be all of one mind in prayer, compassionate, loving the brotherhood, merciful, modest, and humble. Consider it all joy when you fall into various temptations. [Col. 0322D]

Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer. It is necessary to obey God rather than human beings. Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, descending from the Father of lights. Eye has not seen, ear has not heard, nor has it entered the human heart what God has prepared for those who love him. All things are clean to the clean, but to the defiled and faithless nothing is clean. All things are permitted, but not all things are beneficial. A bishop must be blameless, sober, and prudent. The whole life of the faithless is sin. [Col. 0323A]

Idleness is hostile to the soul. Every day must be regarded as the last. The ornaments of the heavens are the virtues of those who preach. A teacher’s word is idle unless the Holy Spirit is present in the heart of the hearer. An idle word is one that lacks either the reason of just necessity or the intention of pious usefulness. Vices are overcome by continual prayer. Those who thirst for earthly riches never deserve to receive spiritual gifts. Every glory and virtue shines less in comparison with something greater. Every divine blow is either a cleansing of the present life or the beginning of punishment to come. [Col. 0323B]

He is altogether mistaken who thinks that he can attain triumph through peace and leisure. Consider yourself an orator if you have persuaded yourself to do what must be done. We misuse the best thing—namely, God’s mercy—in the worst way when, because of his patience, we presume upon every wickedness. Forgetfulness is the greatest fault of the negligent. Opportunities cannot be lacking for those who are perishing. Compliance produces friends; truth produces hatred. Wanton eyes are the betrayers of a luxurious heart. Hidden faults, continually perpetrated, deserve that perverse kings and shepherds be appointed. All the proofs of faith are to be drawn especially from past events. [Col. 0323C]

God is praised and proclaimed better by works than by words. One who strives with an excellent voice but a very evil heart is to be called an enemy, not a faithful friend. Everything that is just may rightly be called one. We must always pray that we not be led astray by the enemy. Be subject to every prelate as to Christ. God has mystically drawn all the things he willed toward himself. From contrasting things we see which are better. O how many cares the mind needs in every hour! A mouth that lies is said to slaughter the soul.

## CHAPTER XV
The Lord is near to all who call upon him in truth. [Col. 0323D] Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his saints. Keep your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit. The patience of the poor will not perish forever. Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you. Everyone will be perfect if he is like his Teacher. God is able to raise up children for Abraham from stones. Strike your son with a rod, and you will deliver his soul from death. Correction benefits the prudent more than a hundred blows benefit a fool.

[Col. 0324A] A prince who willingly listens to words of falsehood has all wicked ministers. The perverse are corrected with difficulty. A weight and a weight, a measure and a measure—both are hateful before God. By the things through which one sins, by those same things one is also tormented. Tested virtue rebukes the foolish. The powerful suffer powerful torments. Because of the sins of the people, the Lord makes a hypocrite reign. The sinner, even if a hundred years old, will be accursed. The whole world will fight against the senseless. Do not follow your desires. Love is the fullness of the law.

[Col. 0324B] The wisdom of the flesh is death, but the wisdom of the spirit is life and peace. Test the spirits, whether they are from God. You ask and do not receive because you ask wrongly. When sin has been completed, it gives birth to death. Through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of God. Let sinners be rebuked before all, so that the others may have fear. Most people follow God with their voices, but flee from him in their conduct. A full belly readily debates about fasts. The proof of love is the display of a deed. Perfect hatred is that which lacks neither justice nor reason.

[Col. 0324C] Those placed amid delights cannot perceive how great eternal punishment is. A peaceful man deserves to be called a son of God. Peace should truly be called such when spirit and flesh are altogether in agreement. The speech of teachers must be shaped according to the character of their hearers. Through the five bodily senses, as through certain windows, entry is given inward to the soul. Some sins stain the soul, while others extinguish it. Parents are to be loved and honored insofar as they themselves are subject to the supreme Father.

[Col. 0324D] The life of the good is always burdensome to those of evil character. Pallor and filth should appear to monks and virgins like precious stones. Whoever is disobedient to his superiors and elders deserves—if he himself should be placed over others—to suffer similar treatment from them. It is a certain advance to recognize, amid punishments, why you deserved punishment. The speech of a chaste mind ought to be chaste. It is part of sacrilege not to give the possessions of the poor to the poor. Those who sinned alike will undergo equal punishment. Public guilt also requires public repentance. True repentance is both to mourn the evils committed and no longer to commit the evils that ought to be mourned.

[Col. 0325A] Those who now refuse to endure small punishments for their crimes will at some time suffer the most severe punishments. All who abandon what is permitted for the love of God must take care lest, living lukewarmly, they fall into what is forbidden. Any shepherd flees when he withdraws consolation from his subjects or, seeing injustice, does not oppose it. Frugal food and a belly always hungry are preferable to three-day fasts. Sin is added to sin when what was wickedly done is also wickedly defended. Deliberate before you promise, lest, when your promises are not fulfilled, you be called a liar. The proof of a holy will is refusing to sin when you are able to do so. The ability to act well or badly is a proof of free choice, [Col. 0325B] and the cause of every merit.

The righteousness of the Pharisees perished through pride, while the unrighteousness of the tax collectors was healed by humility. Danger is never overcome without danger. Those who do well are more worthy of praise than those who speak well. Prudence measures the outcomes of things. Money becomes precious when, transferred to others for the love of God, it ceases to be possessed. Very many strive not to come to poverty; very few labor not to fall into Gehenna. Very many fear disgrace, but few fear the guilt of conscience. There are two kinds of sin: one arising from deliberate intention, the other from negligence.

[Col. 0325C] Be at peace with human beings and at war with vices. One ought to command money, not serve it. Weep now, wretched ones; learn now to shed tears, when it is time to weep, when it is time to have pity. Poverty of the soul is greater than poverty of the body. Let the one who sins strive daily to restore himself immediately. A perfect soldier very often weighs his strength. The prudent acts in everything, doing nothing without a reason. For a perverse mind, its own guilt is the greatest punishment. Do not be quick or too ready to laugh. Whoever is quick to laughter is also said to be quick to anger. An unjust prince has servants who are themselves vicious. Everyone must consider what end awaits him. The more things one attends to, the less perception one has for each individual matter.

[Col. 0325D] The present life is short, but the life to come will be everlasting. Heavenly bread is preferred to all foods.

## CHAPTER XVI

How good God is to Israel, to those who are upright in heart! Seek the Lord and be strengthened; seek his face continually. Seek the Lord, and your soul will live. You who fear the Lord, praise him. You who love the Lord, hate evil. As a father has compassion on his children, so the Lord has had compassion on those who fear him, for he himself knows our formation. Who is like our Lord, who dwells on high and looks upon the lowly in heaven and on earth?

[Col. 0326A] Whoever has not taken his soul in vain and has not sworn deceitfully to his neighbor—he will receive blessing from the Lord and mercy from God his Savior. Those who sow in tears will reap in exultation. Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you. What does it profit a person if he gains the whole world but suffers the loss of his soul? What exchange will a person give for his soul? Whoever is from God hears God’s words. Whoever looks at a woman in order to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.

[Col. 0326B] Whoever perseveres to the end will be saved. What is impossible with human beings is possible with God. Whoever hates his life in this world preserves it for eternal life. What God has joined, let no human separate. Whoever says to his brother, “Fool,” will be liable to the Gehenna of fire. Whoever is unfaithful in the least is also unfaithful in much. To refuse to obey God is like the crime of idolatry. Seek the Lord while he may be found; call upon him while he is near. Whoever turns his ear away so as not to hear the law—his prayer will be accursed.

[Col. 0326C] Whoever follows righteousness is loved by the Lord. Whoever loves discipline loves wisdom. Whoever spares the rod hates his son. Whoever hides his crimes will not prosper, but whoever confesses and abandons them will obtain mercy. Whoever guards his mouth also guards his soul. Whoever offers a sacrifice from the substance of the poor is like one who sacrifices a son in the sight of his father. Like a storm, the wicked passes away. Whoever is inclined to mercy will be blessed. Whoever prepares a pit for his brother will fall into it himself. Whoever is slack and negligent in his work is a brother to one who dissipates his own work.

[Col. 0326D] What you do not gather in youth, how will you be able to possess in old age? What the wicked fears will come upon him. Whoever despises small things will gradually fall. Whatever your hand can do, do it earnestly, for there is neither work, nor reasoning, nor wisdom in the underworld, where you are hastening. Whoever hardens his ear to the cry of the poor will himself cry out and not be heard. Whoever instructs a mocker does himself an injury. Whoever is evil to himself, to whom will he be good? As is the ruler of a city, so are its inhabitants. Those who instruct many in righteousness will be like stars for everlasting eternities.

[Col. 0327A] Whoever offends in one matter loses many good things. Whoever teaches a fool is like one who glues sand together. The greater you are, humble yourself in everything. Those who fear frost will be overtaken by snow. Those who fear God will not be unbelieving toward his word. Those who run in the stadium all run, but one receives the prize. Whoever wishes to be a friend of this world is made an enemy of God. Whoever thinks that he stands must beware lest he fall. Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. Whoever turns a sinner back from the error of his way will save his soul from death.

[Col. 0327B] Whoever does not eat must not judge the one who eats. Whoever does not care for his own, and especially for those of his household, has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever. Whoever is led by the Spirit of God—these are sons of God. Whoever sees his brother suffering need and closes his heart against him, how does the love of God remain in him? Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly. Whoever boasts, let him boast in the Lord. Whatever was written was written for our instruction, so that through the patience and consolation of the Scriptures we might have hope. What you do not wish to be done to you, do not do to another. Whoever is ignorant will be ignored.

[Col. 0327C] Whoever keeps the whole law but offends in one point has become guilty of all. The higher the step, the deeper the fall. What sort of person each one secretly is is shown by the insult inflicted upon him. What praise will we deserve for the pallor of fasting if we are livid with envy? What virtue is there in not drinking wine if one is drunk with anger and hatred? What does it profit to make the body thin through abstinence if the soul swells with pride? Whoever both does some good and yet does not abandon any of his customary pursuits of wickedness is like one who puts his possessions into a pierced bag. Illness shows how great a good health is.

[Col. 0327D] Whoever continually considers how to do some good prays without interruption. How fearful the judgment of divine hardening is can be recognized in the Jews and unbelievers, who were continually hardened. When we complain that we have sinned, we are visited by the Lord. When it pleases us to sin, the devil attacks our heart. Whatever each person wishes to reap, he must first sow. Whoever remembers that he has committed many forbidden acts must also abstain from permitted things as penance.

[Col. 0328A] Whoever considers what he should vow to God should vow himself and give himself. Whatever is a seedbed of pleasure is opposed to chastity. Whoever can come to the aid of one who is perishing, if he does not do so, will be guilty of that person’s death. Whoever can be corrected by gentle words ought not to be irritated by harsh rebuke. Whatever act of compassion is found to have been done by human beings is to be attributed to divine grace. Those who do not have zeal for God lack many virtues. How difficult it is for one to rise whom the weight of evil habit presses down!

[Col. 0328B] However great human righteousness may be, it is nothing compared with divine righteousness. Those who persevere in chastity and virginity become equal to the angels of God. Whatever exceeds measure is suggested by demons. Whatever words of spiritual wisdom pagan men uttered were uttered by God’s providence so that Christians might be instructed not only by their own people but also by outsiders. Insofar as anyone has advanced in humility and chastity, so far will he draw near to God. The more the mind is divided among many activities, the less capable it becomes of each one. The more knowledge is given to each person, the more he is permitted to be tested.

[Col. 0328C] Whoever has never learned to be subject cannot properly rule anyone. What is more wretched than to be distressed by the observed happiness of others? What does it profit someone to be a Cato outwardly when inwardly he is a Nero? What does it profit anyone to walk about in sheep’s clothing if inwardly they carry wolves’ hearts? As long as a person is not displeased with the evils he has committed, vices reign in him. What must be endured altogether, endure patiently. What each person has not experienced in himself, he scarcely believes about another. In as many ways as a person can act badly, in just so many ways he can also act well by abandoning evil.

[Col. 0328D] What it is shameful to do, it is also shameful to say. Whatever each person now reads, as long as the present life remains, whether good or bad, he will always possess it. Whoever has what is sufficient should desire nothing more. Who is rich? The one who desires nothing. And who is poor? The miser. What is characteristic of a fool? Being unable to harm and wishing to do so. What is the work of the prudent? When able, not wishing to harm. How near the shore is in the heart, while the labor of the sea is within. Whoever does not spare himself also knows how to spare no one. How dark is the love by which the Author of light is despised!

[Col. 0329A] What does an effort profit that bears no fruit? What does it profit to seek treasures and lose heaven? How good is the Lord to all who seek him. The more you are able, the more submit yourself to Christ. The one who gives you much also asks the same from you. Whoever God hardens, no one afterward cares for.

## CHAPTER XVII

Your kingdom, Lord, is the kingdom of all ages. Praise befits the upright. Judge rightly, sons of men. The word of the Lord is right, and all his works are in faith.

[Col. 0329B] The Lord will redeem the souls of his servants, and all who hope in him will not offend. Reveal your way to the Lord, hope in him, and he will act. The kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent seize it. A king who sits on the throne of judgment scatters every evil by his gaze. Laughter is mixed with sorrow, and mourning takes possession of the end of joy. A gentle answer breaks anger. A king who judges the poor with truth will have his throne established forever. When the wicked rule, the ruin of human beings will follow.

[Col. 0329C] A just king raises up the land; a greedy man destroys it. The kingdom is transferred from nation to nation because of injustices. Be renewed in the spirit of your mind and put on the new person, who was created according to God in the justice and holiness of truth. Pure and undefiled religion before God the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their tribulation. The root of all evils is greed. Evil priests are the ruin of the people. The kingdom of God is worth as much as you possess. A religious person, if he becomes angry quickly, is also easily corrected.

[Col. 0329D] A person who judges another’s merits rightly cannot do so when his own conscience provides no standard of judgment through innocence. Humble married people follow the Lamb more rightly than proud virgins. Those strong in body, unless they devoutly serve God, from whom they have their strength, will suffer punishments for this. Whatever more than animals a human being possesses must be referred to divine compassion. As often as human reason resists perverse thoughts, so many heavenly crowns does it deserve. The governance of souls is the art of arts. Leniency and inappropriate gentleness are reckoned before God as great cruelty. The first resurrection is to rise from vices in this life.

[Col. 0330A] Let the one who does not wish to be condemned rise in the first resurrection. Those who seize the property of others will themselves one day be seized for destruction. Sudden fury has no reason. Those who rebel against divine mercy will be handed over to diabolical power. Every obscure matter should be explained by means of a comparison. The reprobate are wearied in this age by desires and in the future by torments. The rustic speech of men who retain a gentle heart is more pleasing to the Lord than the learned speech of the proud. A pious and just king strives to be what he is called. Alas, faith is rarely to be granted to anyone!

[Col. 0330B] The perfect ruler first rules his own actions. The person of a king admonishes the king toward better things. The violent customarily seize the kingdom of heaven. In adverse circumstances, do not let yourself be deprived of composure.

## CHAPTER XVIII

Serve the Lord in fear, and rejoice before him with trembling. A sacrifice to God is a contrite spirit. May the glory of the Lord endure forever and ever. The salvation of the just is from the Lord, and he is their protector in time of tribulation. May the name of the Lord be blessed from this time forth and forever. The Lord is gracious to all, and his mercy is over all his works.

[Col. 0330C] The Spirit breathes where he wills, and you hear his voice, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth. If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you. God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, so that everyone who believes in him might not perish but have eternal life. If your brother sins against you, go and rebuke him between you and him alone. The eyes of the wise are in his head. The Holy Spirit of discipline will flee from deceit and withdraw from thoughts that lack understanding.

[Col. 0330D] Think of the Lord in goodness and seek him in simplicity of heart. The wise and understanding heart abstains from sins. Folly is bound up in the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline will drive it away. A fool is not corrected by words. The simplicity of the upright will guide them, and the treachery of the perverse will destroy them. A deceitful balance is an abomination before God, but an accurate weight is his will. The wise person remains like the sun, but the fool changes like the moon. The wise person seeks out the wisdom of all the ancients.

[Col. 0331A] Hidden wisdom and an unseen treasure—what use are either of them? The wise person makes himself known by few words. God speaks once, and does not repeat it a second time. The hope of the hypocrite will perish. The just falls seven times and rises again, but the wicked will fall into evil. The fool raises his voice in laughter. It is good to conceal the secrets of a king, but it is honorable to reveal the mighty works of God. Dreams exalt the imprudent. If we live by the spirit, let us also walk by the spirit. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love is perfected in us. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

[Col. 0331B] If anyone says, “Because I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar. The spiritual person judges all things, but is himself judged by no one. If someone does not know how to govern his own household, how will he care for the church of God? The wisdom of this world is foolishness before God. Just as all die in Adam, so all will be made alive in Christ. The gifts and calling of God are without repentance. A servant of God ought not to quarrel, but to be gentle toward all. Star differs from star in glory, and so also is the resurrection of the dead. Whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.

[Col. 0331C] Human beings are to be loved in such a way that their errors are not loved. A watchman stands above, observing us and our deeds every day. To know is to approve in God’s case; not to know is to reject. The highest nobility before God is to be distinguished by virtues. To escape the snares of Satan depends not on the one who wills or the one who runs, but on God who has mercy. The faults of subjects are sometimes to be concealed, but afterward, because they were concealed, they are to be disclosed. Those who do not resist good people openly but slander them as soon as they have withdrawn may be called scorpions. Whoever wishes to live with the innocent seeks solitude.

[Col. 0331D] The salvation of the rich lies in helping the needs of the poor. The virtue of patience repels the arrows of insult. He denies himself who, abandoning the person of carnal life, puts on the spiritual and new person—that is, Christ. The visible sacrifice is the sacrament of sacrifice. Devotion to worldly studies quickly causes people to go astray on the way of God. The warfare of the spiritual life consists chiefly in love and patience. Possessing the name of holiness without works benefits no one.

[Col. 0332A] It is utter folly if we seek to please those whom we know displease God. Bodily health and beauty scarcely accept the form of humility. The wise person is the one who strives to teach others more by deeds than by words. Whoever sets no end to sinning in his heart deserves to be tormented without end. It is enough for each person to argue or dictate in such a way that he is understood. Excess, both of words and of other things, must be avoided. Whoever is devoted to secular literature cannot grasp the mysteries of sacred Scripture. When reading sacred Scripture, one must attend to what is said mystically or according to the letter, what is said in part or for the whole.

[Col. 0332B] The meaning must be weighed together with the words of sacred Scripture. Meditation on sacred Scripture draws the mind back from harmful thoughts. Comparisons of various things should continually be offered for our edification, in this manner: Just as a dog returns to its vomit, so the imprudent repeats his folly. Just as water extinguishes fire, so almsgiving extinguishes sin. Just as many foods are of no benefit without salt, so all virtues are of no benefit without love. Just as a pipe produces no sound without someone blowing into it, so the human heart receives no good without divine inspiration.

[Col. 0332C] Just as the running of horses is tested in an open place, so the will of a human being is tested in the freedom granted to it. Just as everyone’s eyes are in the head, so every intention of the faithful must rest in Christ. The ministers of the supreme ruler must first of all be provided for. Pride alone corrupts all good things. Our sense is drawn toward the desire of the one whose pleasure captures it. The servant of God ought to love divine books more than gems and silk. The bodily senses are like horses running without reason; the soul, however, like a charioteer, holds the reins of those who run.

[Col. 0332D] It is a consolation for the wicked to criticize the life of the good. Priests and clerics are not permitted to attend spectacles. Forgive others in the way you wish them to forgive you when you sin. Whatever object is more precious must be guarded with correspondingly greater care. Blood touches blood when sins are added to sins. Whoever possesses worldly substance must bring the needy into his house and refresh them. If you love to be called father and prince, preserve the name with honor and fulfill it in your conduct.

[Col. 0333A] The great pine is often shaken by the winds, and lofty towers fall with a heavier crash. Foolish vows must be broken. Without instruction, life is like an image of death. Equal concern must be maintained for those standing and those fallen: for the former, so that they do not fall backward; for the latter, so that they may rise quickly. Speech is given to many, wisdom of spirit to few. If you cannot help many, at least care for yourself alone. If you have vowed anything to the Lord, do not delay in paying it. It belongs to the Lord alone to bring good things from evil. Whoever despises counsel will often suffer danger. We often desire a good thing that we soon show we do not want.

[Col. 0333B] The miser is always in need; no amount of money fills him. If you wish to be saved, put nothing before this salvation. There are far too few who rightly wish to have mercy. The spirit is life; the philosophy of the flesh is death.

## CHAPTER XIX

A hymn befits you, O God, in Zion, and a vow will be paid to you in Jerusalem. The testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to the simple. To you, Lord, the poor person is abandoned; you will be the helper of the orphan. Fear God, all his saints, for there is no want for those who fear him. Store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither rust nor moth destroys, and where thieves do not break in [Col. 0333C] or steal. A desirable treasure rests in the mouth of the wise. The fool pours out his whole spirit, but the wise person delays and reserves something for the future. The fear of the Lord drives out sin. There is a time for every matter under heaven. The name of the Lord is a very strong tower; the just person runs to it and will be exalted. A threefold cord is not easily broken. A false witness will not go unpunished. There is fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear. It is shameful that someone who does not know how to hold the reins of his own life should become judge of another’s.

[Col. 0333D] The more subtly a person judges matters of darkness, the more truly the brightness of light illuminates him. All earthly things are lost by preserving them, but preserved by giving them away. Let the one who prepares a house of the mind for God wipe away the filth of evil conduct. We bear the evils of the world more tolerably if we are armed against them with the shield of foreknowledge. To hide the talent in the earth is to entangle an ability received in earthly activities. Each person carries his neighbor insofar as he loves him. Whoever offered himself gave everything to God.

[Col. 0334A] The fear of God and continual prayer make a person fly toward heavenly things. The ever-watchful tempter strikes with sharper snares those whom he sees most abstaining from sins. Vices are worse insofar as they are concealed beneath the appearance of virtues. Christians who live lukewarmly are corrected with greater difficulty than pagans. The excessively grasping and the excessively lavish both flow together into one vice of excess. Everything temperate is acceptable both to God and to human beings. Very tender minds must be formed by more rigorous exercises. The torments of some benefit others for correction.

[Col. 0334B] Whoever does not know how to be silent does not know how to speak either. The one whose power is over all must be feared above all. Touching other people’s bodies and burning desire for women draw the mind toward madness. A person errs in faith as long as he distrusts that everything is seen and governed by God. It is difficult to help those who remain silent; but those who confess the nature of their illness will more easily receive healing. Evils offer us opportunities to do good as often as, seeing or hearing them, we disregard them. The more holy a profession someone makes, the more carefully he must beware of being deceived by pride.

[Col. 0334C] Each person can despise as much as he can also desire. Such is the nature of vices that, unless past sins are erased by swift repentance, others arise from them. Concealed hatreds are worse than open ones. Let us be inwardly what we show ourselves outwardly. As fire tests gold glowing like a furnace, so God will purify the elect in the fire of suffering. It is shameful for a teacher when the fault rebukes him himself. Fear that you will fall when you see another falling. Consider yourself injured when you see anyone suffering. Whoever longs for earthly things scarcely believes in spiritual ones. No one who suffers from suspicion will ever be safe.

[Col. 0334D] Those whose hope is placed in the depths are easily saddened. A truthful witness remains suitable for a true king. The anger of a king is a great storm. Being wholly present everywhere, he is to be worshiped with all one’s strength.

## CHAPTER XX

All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth for those who seek his covenant and testimonies. The face of the Lord is against those who do evil, to destroy their memory from the earth. The Lord will seek truth and repay abundantly those who act arrogantly. Human help is vain. The heavens were established by the word of the Lord, and all their power by the breath of his mouth.

[Col. 0335A] Act manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, all you who hope in the Lord. Men of bloodshed and deceit will not divide their days. A talkative man will not prosper on the earth; evil will seize the unjust man in his destruction. The voice of exultation and salvation is in the tents of the just. Watch at all times, praying that you may be considered worthy to escape the things that are to come. Watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. Woe to you who tithe mint, dill, and cumin, and have abandoned the weightier matters—that is, mercy and judgment. Every tree is known by its fruit.

[Col. 0335B] Foxes have dens and the birds of heaven nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head. Where your treasure is, there also is your heart. The words of the wise are like goads and like nails driven firmly into place. The words of flatterers are soft, but they strike the innermost parts of the belly. All human beings are vain in whom there is no knowledge of God. The voice of the day of the Lord is bitter; there the strong man will be troubled. Wine and women make even the wise apostatize. Woe to the city whose king is a boy and whose princes eat in the morning! Where there is pride, there will also be insult.

[Col. 0335C] An angry man provokes quarrels, but the patient man calms those that have been stirred up. Woe to the solitary, because when he falls he has no one to raise him up. Woe to those who call good evil and evil good! The way of the wicked is dark; they do not know where they will fall. The way of life belongs to the one who guards discipline; whoever abandons reproof goes astray. Anger kills the foolish man, and envy slays the little one. The health of the heart is the life of the flesh, but envy is the rottenness of the bones. The furnace tests the potter’s vessels, and the trial of tribulation tests just people.

[Col. 0335D] A good word is above the best gift. A sweet word multiplies friends and soothes enemies. One Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all. The manifestation of the Spirit is given to each person for the common good. Each will receive his own reward according to his labor. A person is perfected in weakness. Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. A person divided in mind is unstable in all his ways.

[Col. 0336A] Where there is love and affection, there is the assembly of the saints. The final tribulation is preceded by many tribulations. True discernment is acquired only through true humility. Food and clothing ought to be the riches of Christians. The person who keeps the eyes of his mind open to the sight of the true light is vigilant. An undivided will to do good will be reckoned by God as the deed of beneficence. The will of God is his work: for he spoke, and they were made. A good will must be obtained above all.

[Col. 0336B] Each virtue is so much lesser insofar as the other virtues are absent. Vices must first be uprooted from a person, and then virtues planted. God is to be revered not only for his immense power but also for his immeasurable clemency. Virgins and monks should regulate their fasting so that they are always strong for the service of God. Virtue is always exposed to envy. When one pestilent person is scourged, many perverse people are corrected. Every pleasure, like bees, after pouring out pleasant honey, wounds hearts with its sting. Pleasure has punishment, and necessity produces a crown.

[Col. 0336C] The fever of the soul is more violent than that of the body. That traveler is foolish who, seeing pleasant meadows along the road, forgets where he was going. Where there is no fear of God, there the kingdom of sin is. The wise person places the fruit of virtue in conscience; the less perfect person places it in glory. Whoever is overcome by one vice quickly falls into another. The seeker of empty glory resembles one who entrusts his seeds to be scattered by the wind. Whoever wishes to preserve his health should despise or mock no one’s weakness. Those devoted to vices cannot be enriched with virtues. Pride must be avoided: it deceived even the angels and destroys all virtues. From the source where the good person prospers, the envious person wastes away.

[Col. 0336D] The physician who knows how to give no medicines except mild ones is very inexperienced. As kings wish, so laws have force. Scarcely anyone passes into goodness except from evil. Those who are unwilling to endure any adversity are excessively delicate. Whoever casts away shame casts away all virtues at once. Empty speech and vain thought destroy much peace. Leisure gives the mind instability. Woe to those who presume to believe themselves so wise that they need no admonitions from anyone else!

[Col. 0337A] They are deceived in every way who think that they can penetrate the teachings of sacred law with carnal understanding. Silver is cheaper than gold; gold is cheaper than virtues. If you do not know how to live rightly, withdraw and yield to those who do. Great usefulness lies hidden even in small things. Love of usefulness quickly advises what must be done. Fine clothing makes the heart animal-like. The one who is now altogether proud will have to be pressed down severely. The person who has long kept company with evil is scarcely corrected.

[Col. 0338A] Various virtues can dwell together. It is a great virtue to bless in return for curses. Every person is like a stone unless he is softened by the Most High. A man is constituted more by the strength of his spirit than by what you see. Great strength of spirit is to be moved by no one’s praise. The more things are lowly, the more precious they are in mystery. The one living in Christ stands confidently in him. A man acting wisely is like the sun to others, shining brightly.

[Col. 0337]

## A SERMON OF THE SAME OTHLO ON THE FEAST OF THE APOSTLES

Extracted from the autograph manuscript of the illustrious monastery of Saint Emmeram at Regensburg by the Reverend Father Caspar Altlechner, Benedictine of Melk.

(In Reverend Father Bernard Pez’s *Thesaurus Anecdotorum Novissimus*, volume III, part II, p. 537.)

[Col. 0337B] Since, therefore, all the choirs of the holy martyrs and confessors throughout the whole world are rightly worthy of veneration, we nevertheless believe that the apostles are worthy of greater veneration, since, having first been chosen by our Lord Jesus Christ, they were granted the privilege of enjoying his bodily presence. Indeed, they are believed to be the leaders of the churches not only because they first established them in this world, as founders, by teaching and writing the Lord’s commandments, but also because they will be the first judges on the day of judgment, as the Lord himself testifies when he says to them: “Amen, amen, I say to you, you who have followed me: in the regeneration, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of his majesty, you also will sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel” (Matthew 19:28).

Likewise, in another place he speaks [Col. 0337C] to them, saying: “I assign to you, just as my Father assigned to me, a kingdom, so that you may eat and drink at my table and sit upon thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel” (Luke 22:29–30). But they are also to be embraced with the greatest veneration for this reason: the power of binding and loosing human sins—which is believed to have been granted in part to other saints as well—appears to have been assigned to the apostles in a special way above all others, since the Lord says: “Amen I say to you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven” (Matthew 18:18).

Besides these matters, then, which we have already said were spoken commonly to all twelve disciples of Christ, certain things can be found written not only in the Gospel but also in the Acts [Col. 0337D] of the Apostles and scattered through ecclesiastical histories, which apply to the individual persons among them. Through all these things it is proved that the apostles possessed a special grace of virtues and that in them was fulfilled most especially what our Savior is read to have said to them: “Amen I say to you, whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do, and will do greater works than these” (John 14:12).

For, to say nothing of the other miracles of blessed Peter, prince of the apostles, it is enough to mention this one: the sick were placed in the streets so that, when he arrived, at least his shadow might overshadow them, and they might be freed from their illnesses (Acts 5:15). Since this is never read to have been done by our Lord, blessed Peter, truly believing in him according to his promise, performed a miracle greater than Christ’s. To whom, I ask, did he reserve something of this kind, if not to a disciple?

We believe that what we have said about one apostle applies also to the others, even though we may not have read all their deeds: each of them possessed some miraculous gift. For although he has given many gifts to all who believe in him, he granted special gifts to the apostles whom he himself had instructed bodily. Since, however, we cannot recount the special virtues of every disciple, we bring forward certain deeds handed down to our memory in connection with their respective feasts and praises, which we judge ought to be celebrated above those of others.

After Peter, Paul rightly deserves to be mentioned first. Although he was not counted among the twelve apostles whom Jesus Christ chose bodily, it is nevertheless clear that, by a heavenly calling and wondrous teaching, he was received among the apostolic company and ranks with equal merit. This seems especially evident because, at the same time as blessed Peter began to preach, Paul too became a preacher and deserved to share with him one and the same day and place of martyrdom.

Blessed Paul so far surpassed almost all men in the sublimity of his special virtues that, through the abundance and wisdom of his preaching, he was called the Doctor and Teacher of many nations (1 Tim. 2:7). Moreover, because of the purity of his life, while he was still in the flesh he was caught up as far as the third heaven (2 Cor. 12:2).

From there let us pass, with particular praise, to Andrew, who was Peter’s brother and, together with him, deserved to be called by our Savior: “Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of men” (Matt. 4:19). He later carried out this fishing all the more effectively and wisely because he had been predestined for it by the Master of all. For, as trustworthy histories relate, he won over to the Lord, through the nets of his preaching, a very great multitude of people in the province of Achaia; and for this very cause he ultimately endured the gallows of the cross by dying.

We have added this in order to show in him some special privilege of grace: for it was a great thing that he deserved to be made like Christ through death on the cross.

[Col. 0339B] Next, the elder James is to be honored with praise—namely, the brother of John the Evangelist. Both were sons of Zebedee, and both were chosen together by the Lord immediately after blessed Peter and his brother Andrew. Moreover, as the Gospel relates, after their mother came to Jesus and asked that one of them sit at his right hand and the other at his left, the Lord answered them: “You do not know what you are asking.” Then he asked both of them: “Can you drink the cup that I am about to drink?” When they answered, “We can,” they immediately heard: “You shall drink my cup” (Matt. 20:21–23).

In this drinking of the cup, which is understood as imitation of the Lord’s Passion, we believe that this James of whom we speak possessed a great privilege of merit, because he was the first of the apostles to complete the triumph of martyrdom.

After him, his brother John, no lesser in merit although later in number, is to be praised: God’s chosen virgin and greatest evangelist. He is so specially crowned with the charisms of virtue that we think human reason can express nothing worthy of him. Nevertheless, since we cannot speak adequately of the special privilege of his virtues, we do not therefore think that his miracles should be entirely left unmentioned. Perhaps our very inadequacy constitutes the greatness of his praise.

O how worthy of reverence is the fact that he was specially loved by the Lord, and that, when the Lord was already dying on the cross, he entrusted to this virgin his Mother—the ever-virgin Mary. Who would not also judge worthy of veneration in him the fact that, when he had been exiled to the island of Patmos, he deserved both to penetrate the secrets of heaven by vision and to disclose them to the world in writing?

There is also a privilege not inferior to these: formerly entreated by the holy Fathers of Asia, he suppressed, through the Gospel of the divine word, all the deceits of the heretics that had erupted at that time. Thus, after completing the course of his present life, he is said to have entered his tomb while still alive and to have closed his final day there, not by dying but as though by falling asleep. Let anyone who wishes turn each of these matters over in his mind, and then he will recognize that such things were granted to the disciples alone.

Thomas too perhaps contains special crowns, because, by touching with his own hands the true flesh and wounds of our Lord after his resurrection, he drove the diseases of unbelief from all the faithful (John 20:27–28).

The other James also clearly deserves veneration—namely, the one whom Holy Scripture calls both “just,” because of the purity of his life, and “the brother of the Lord” (Gal. 1:19), because of his bodily relationship to him. He is therefore said to have been the son of the sister of Saint Mary the Virgin. Besides the aforementioned kinship with our Savior, in which he possessed a sufficiently great and special distinction, he grew from his mother’s womb into such excellence of merit that he drank neither wine nor strong drink, ate none of the customary flesh of animals, did not anoint himself with oil, and did not use baths.

Nor does Matthew, recalled from the tax office, lack special gifts of virtue. For he deserved at once to feed the Lord whom he had called as a guest in the lodging of his own house; and, having been transformed from a tax collector into an evangelist, he offered all believers the greatest hope of conversion.

Luke and Mark too are rich and distinguished through their composition of the Gospel, although they are reported to have been outside the number of the Twelve. Nevertheless, they are all the more worthy of veneration because, through God’s providence, they are recognized as appointed witnesses of the truth. And you, holy Matthias, chosen by a pious lot, are rightly venerated by all mortals, since you contain a great privilege of sanctity.

Of the four remaining men who belong to the number of the twelve apostles—namely, Philip, whose memory is celebrated in the Gospel and whose feast is observed together with that of the younger James; Bartholomew, who is said to have been sent to farther India; and Simon and Judas, who was surnamed Thaddeus and was the brother of the James mentioned immediately above—of these, I say, although we are unworthy, we may learn something of the miracles of their virtues, apart from their passions, which they share in some measure with the other saints.

Nevertheless, we ought with special veneration to praise and honor not only all twelve disciples but also the other seventy-two, because our Savior deemed them worthy to illuminate them above all other human beings through his election and teaching. For the less fittingly we are able to venerate him himself, who is wholly above all and wholly present in all, the more diligently let us devote ourselves to the praises and feasts of his saints, especially the apostles, so that through their intercession we may deserve to obtain forgiveness of sins and to be delivered from the various dangers of soul and body that already threaten us.

For since the most wicked enemy now sets greater snares for us than in former times, what sufficient remedy can we find against him except to seek and invoke the aid of our chief intercessors as well? A great enemy is forcefully subdued by a mighty slaughter.

Therefore, dearest brothers and fathers, as we celebrate the feast-days of whichever of Christ’s apostles we may be honoring, let us imitate to some extent their teaching and their virtues, so that they themselves may defend us from the dangers of the present life and, at the future and fearful judgment, where they will become judges, decree that we, separated from the wicked, be placed among the good. This is granted by our Lord Jesus Christ, who with the Father and the Holy Spirit reigns forever, throughout the endless ages.

[Col. 0341]

THE BOOK OF VISIONS OF OTHLO, MONK OF THE MONASTERY OF SAINT EMMERAM, OF THE ORDER OF SAINT BENEDICT, BOTH HIS OWN AND THOSE OF OTHERS. Now first brought to light from the author’s own manuscript, preserved in the imperial monastery of Saint Emmeram at Regensburg, by the Reverend Father Ludwig Moidinqs, Benedictine of Melk.

(In the Reverend Father Bernard Pez’s *Thesaurus Anecdotorum*, unpublished material, vol. III, part II, p. 545.)

BEGINNING OF OTHLO’S PROLOGUE

[Col. 0341A] Our Lord and Savior, presenting many first elements of perfection to those striving toward perfection, also taught among these things that even the slower and poorer in either aspect of the human person should not therefore utterly despair of their salvation if they could not attain the summit of virtue, saying: “Whoever gives a cup of cold water in my name shall not lose his reward” (Matt. 10:42).

I think that these words are to be understood not only according to the letter but also spiritually. For I believe that, just as one who, because of the smallness of his means, gives a needy person the smallest portion of alms—that is, a cup of cold water—will receive a reward, so also one who is supported by no resources of suitable learning, but gathers from various places fragments or crumbs fallen from the table of the learned and offers some little words of edification, may deserve some reward.

[Col. 0341B] Encouraged, therefore, by this faith and hope, I wish to present for the edification of the faithful certain visions through which the Lord once deigned to admonish me, or which I learned from the reports of other faithful people.

By “visions” I mean not only those that we see in peaceful or troubled dreams—when, carried away in spirit, we sense ourselves undergoing various disturbances or scourges—but also those that many customarily behold while awake or placed at the point of death. All these kinds of visions are found in many forms in Holy Scripture, but especially those related by blessed Gregory in the fourth book of the *Dialogues*. I have imitated his purpose in this little work.

[Col. 0341C] I beg that no one undervalue these accounts either because of my insignificance or because of the rusticity of the account itself. Rather, let each person attend to what I have put forth for the common edification, in whatever unpolished language. Often a pleasant drink can be drawn from a cheap vessel.

And O unhappy people who despise the warnings of divine mercy! Through them God deigns to recall not only the wakeful but also those given over to sleep—now by the gentlest admonition or by exhortation beyond ordinary human measure, now by showing the dreadful punishments of hell and the final judgment itself as though it were impending, and sometimes, when he sees that no amendment results from the gentleness of the visions mentioned above, by the severity of immense blows, recalling them from wantonness and deadly torpor.

I know that all these things must be guarded against with all the greater caution and believed with all the greater truth, because I myself have learned them by experience. For I confess my sin: no one was more doubtful than I about warnings of this kind, until I was brought to faith by the most savage torments, as will be explained below. But what wonder is it if almighty God can visit and admonish people at rest in this way, when we also read that he did the same to certain holy men who were still living in this life?

Having thus prefaced these matters, let us approach the subject itself. I earnestly beg those who, on reading this, know that any of these things happened otherwise than they are told—for many of the people from whose reports I learned them are still living—to correct them and restore them to the pure truth, if something has slipped from my memory or was related to me differently from the way it occurred.

As for what I endeavor to report about myself, and what I wish above all to say at the beginning as an introduction to what follows, God, in whose sight we all stand, knows that I do not wish to state anything otherwise than I saw or experienced, except insofar as I may omit something for the sake of brevity or because it seemed unrelated to edification.

BEGINNING OF THE BOOK OF VISIONS

[Col. 0343]
